name: Low TV Console / Media Cabinet
pitch: A long, low media console with open bays, rear cable slots and a cleat-ready rail, raised so the robot vacuum goes underneath. Cut to the width of your wall.

stages.title: Cut the sheet(s)
stages.detail: Run the fit-test coupon first (slot = tab + 0.1 mm), then cut 1 sheet(s) from the DXFs (CUT layer): 28 m of path. Inside-out order, air assist on. The 1500 mm-class TOP and BOTTOM are the longest parts on the bed.

stages.title: Remove char and sand
stages.detail: Brush char from the cut edges, 120 then 180 grit on faces and edges; ease the top corners. Wipe with a damp rag.

stages.title: Dry fit
stages.detail: Stand SIDE-L and SIDE-R, push BOTTOM, the 2 divider(s) and both rails into place, then lower TOP over all the tabs. Check square and that TOP sits flat. No glue yet.

stages.title: Pre-finish the inside faces
stages.detail: Seal / oil the bay faces and the rail faces before glue-up (mask tabs and slots so the glue still bonds). Two coats on all faces is easiest done flat.

stages.title: Glue-up (Titebond III)
stages.detail: Lay SIDE-L flat. Glue and tap in BOTTOM, the divider(s), RAIL-BOT and RAIL-TOP, fit SIDE-R and clamp. Last, seat TOP on every tab with a few light taps from a block. Work in two halves if alone (10 minute open time).

stages.title: Screws as clamps
stages.detail: 10 #8 x 1-1/2 in screws (3.0 mm pilots cut in): through each side face into the BOTTOM edge, and down through TOP into the side and divider edges. Countersink and plug the top screws.

stages.title: Cable slots, TV strap, optional cleat
stages.detail: Feed cables through the 3 rear slots. Fit the TV anti-tip strap through the 6 mm holes in RAIL-TOP into a stud. Optional wall-hung version: Z-bar cleat across RAIL-TOP into studs; heavy (rated load unverified), so only with a proper stud-rated cleat and an empty-console test first.

stages.title: Finish, test, pack
stages.detail: Two coats of water-based poly or hardwax oil, 24 h cure, 40 kg weight test on TOP, felt pads under the 4 feet, flat-pack in one 1.55 x 0.45 x 0.15 m box with corner guards.

materials.sheet: 18 mm (3/4 in) birch or Baltic-birch plywood, 4 x 8 ft (1220 x 2440 mm) x 1

hardware.note: TV to wall; recommended on every console

hardware.item: Aluminum Z-bar French cleat, 36 in pair
hardware.note: optional wall-hung version, studs only; laser cannot cut the 45 deg bevel

materials.finish: water-based poly or hardwax oil, 2 coats (about $16)

safety: Strap the TV to the wall (anti-tip strap); a low console does not stop a TV tipping off it.
Rated target 40 kg TV (88 lb) on the top, UNVERIFIED - load test one unit to 60 kg before selling; keep each bay <= 650 mm.
Not a clothing-storage unit (STURDY Act applies to dressers >= 27 in); not a children's product (no CPSIA testing).
Wall-hung (cleat) use only into studs with a stud-rated cleat; test empty then loaded.
Keep AV gear ventilated: the open bays and rear slots are for that; do not box it in.

profit.labels: ESTIMATES AND ASSUMPTIONS ONLY - not quotes, not guaranteed, machine time NOT measured on the real machine
profit.assumptions: All dollar figures are planning ESTIMATES / ASSUMPTIONS, not quotes, not guaranteed. Sheet prices: 4x8 ft 18 mm birch plywood $70-110, basic plywood $55-75 (assumption). Machine time uses a sourced RANGE for a 120 W diode on 18 mm ply (low 120 / typical 300 / high 600 mm/min effective, i.e. after multiple passes; see CUT-SPEED-RESEARCH.md); ACMER publishes no 18 mm ply feed rate, so none of it is measured on this machine. Machine wear/electricity $1.70 per machine-hour (assumption). Labor valued at $25/h for the "after labor" line only. Marketplace fees 10% (assumption, e.g. Etsy-style).

machine_time.label: ESTIMATE. Diode = ACMER X1 Ultra 120 W on 18 mm plywood; effective rate = speed / passes. Includes rapid travel between contours and 15 min per sheet of load/focus/unload. Not measured.

commercial_laser.label: ASSUMPTION. Sourced case: 300-600 W CO2 flatbed, single pass at ~600 mm/min (vendor 480-720), 60 m/min rapids, 5 min/sheet, $8/h operating cost. What-if cases: a machine 10x / 20x faster than the diode mid cut+travel time (not sourced for 18 mm ply).

profit.price_band_source: My estimate: Etsy/web plywood media consoles roughly $200-$700 and Amazon 55-65 in particle-board units about $120-$250 (third-party, not verified here). A wall-fitted solid-ply console with cable slots and bays is priced above the commodity units; low = 1200 mm unfinished, high = 2000 mm finished.
profit.note_machine_time: ESTIMATE: 1.9 h (low-speed case 4.2 h, best case 1.1 h) of machine time per unit for 28 m of cut path in 1 sheet(s) on a 120 W diode, 18 mm plywood. Machine time, not material, is still the limit on profit per hour, but a single test cut on scrap will replace this range with a real number.

unverified: Machine time is an estimate (120 W diode on 18 mm ply, sourced range, not measured on this machine); cut time and profit/hour depend on it.
Top sag is a hand calculation (assumed ply modulus); a long span with a heavy TV needs a physical load test.
Wall-hung cleat capacity of an aluminum Z-bar on a console this size is unverified.
No doors or drawers are modeled; the TOP overhangs 20 mm on every side.
Price band is my estimate, not a market quote.
